title: Home Care vs. Assisted Living: An Honest Side-by-Side Comparison
description: Should Mom stay home with help, or move to assisted living? Here's an honest look at home care, assisted living, memory care and nursing homes: typical monthly costs, privacy, pets, couples, one-on-one care, flexibility, and when home care isn't the right fit.
end: We'd rather you choose well than choose us.

parts.head: Home care vs. assisted living
parts.text: Should Mom stay at home with help, or move to assisted living? It's one of the hardest decisions a family makes. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's an honest, side-by-side look, including when home care isn't the right fit.

parts.head: Four main choices
parts.sub: Home care, assisted living, memory care, nursing home
parts.text: There are four main options: home care, assisted living, memory care, and a nursing home. Each one fits a different need.

parts.head: Typical monthly costs
parts.text: Let's start with cost. Assisted living typically runs about thirty-five hundred to fifty-five hundred dollars a month. Memory care, about five thousand to seventy-five hundred. A nursing home, about sixty-five hundred to nine thousand. And home care depends on the hours, from about thirty-six hundred dollars a month, to over fourteen thousand for care around the clock.

parts.head: Stay in their own home
parts.sub: Full privacy, their pets, couples together
parts.text: Home care is the only option where they stay in their own home, with full privacy. They keep their pets, and couples can always stay together.

parts.head: One-on-one, and flexible
parts.text: With home care, the caregiver is one-on-one with your loved one, not shared among other residents. And the plan is flexible. You can adjust the hours any time.

parts.head: A built-in community
parts.sub: Some help, and more people around
parts.text: Assisted living can be a great fit for someone who needs some help and wants more people around. There's a built-in community, though rooms may be shared, and pets are only sometimes allowed.

parts.head: Secured, memory-focused care
parts.sub: For dementia that needs secured supervision
parts.text: Memory care is for dementia that needs secured supervision, with structured, memory-focused days. Couples can usually stay together only if both need memory care.

parts.head: Skilled nursing, full time
parts.text: A nursing home has skilled nursing on site, full time. It's the right fit for complex medical needs.

parts.head: When home care isn't the right fit
parts.sub: Round-the-clock skilled nursing, or an unsafe home
parts.text: And here's when we'd tell you home care isn't the right fit. If round-the-clock skilled nursing is medically necessary, if the home itself can't be made safe, or if full-time supervision plus medical staff is needed and family can't be involved at all, a nursing facility or memory care community is often the more responsible choice.

parts.head: Home care is non-medical
parts.sub: Daily life help. Reminders, not giving medicines.
parts.text: Home care, like ours, is non-medical. Caregivers help with daily life: bathing, dressing, meals, getting around, and company. They remind about medicines, but don't give them.

parts.head: It isn't always either-or
parts.sub: Start with a few hours, and add as needs change
parts.text: And it isn't always either-or. Many families start with a few hours of help at home, and add more as needs change. We'd rather you choose well than choose us.
Not sure which fits? Call us at (417) 234-8494, and we'll talk it through, honestly. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
